notes.title: Dev Diary 33#
notes.notes:
[p][b]Dear Earthlings[/b]   

After a personally successful sales period, I'm now diving into the next exciting update, the RPG update! I've got some interesting things to show and tell you, so here we go![/p][p]
[b]Automation
[/b]I'm planning to add automation to the game. This feature is still highly experimental, and I'm not yet sure if it will make it into the final version, but the tests I've been running are looking very promising. [/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="2IvEgDjBYdo;full"][/previewyoutube][p]

The idea behind automation is to make crafting more engaging and challenging, while also reducing grind. With automation, you'll be able to move items along conveyor belts and through stations. For example, if you connect a conveyor belt from a cargo crate to a shaper station, it will automatically pick up any filtered ore from the crate and send it into the shaper for processing. Then, if you connect another conveyor belt from the shaper to a different cargo crate, the processed ore will be sent back into storage automatically.[/p][p]This system should make shipbuilding a lot more interesting as well.


[b]Ship/base building
[/b]I'm also making major improvements to the spaceship and base building mechanics. I’ve received some very valuable feedback from you all, pointing out that building currently feels tedious and not very fun,  so I’m ramping up the entire building experience.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41812483/9cc3e4c6b807329665cf37f417e83e441ec7b107.png"][/img][/p][p]One major change is the addition of rooms. Players will need to designate dedicated rooms within their ship or base, each with required objects in order to function properly. These rooms can also be assigned to specific crew members, making ship and base building feel much more personal and meaningful.[/p][p]Another big change: I'm removing individual object items. Instead, crafting will happen directly through the build menu and will no longer rely on what's in your personal inventory. The system will automatically check your cargo for the required materials, making the building process smoother and more intuitive.[/p][p]These changes should greatly improve the building aspect of the game.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41812483/d567c2a2a1829eb796c84d74cb0b307509d2e967.png"][/img][/p][p][b]FIRE!
[/b]That's not all, I'm also working on implementing a fire mechanic, so your spaceship or base can actually catch fire. And yes, enemy ships and bases can burn too, of course.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41812483/10a8ea78a35e7923b754c2022c531d264ea6f318.png"][/img][/p][p]I'm planning to add a flamethrower weapon, and I’ve already implemented a fire extinguisher. Naturally, the fire extinguisher can be used to put out fires, but it also doubles as a tool to stun NPCs. Just be aware, they don’t like it when you do that.  [/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="iNnSdYGfh6A;full"][/previewyoutube][p]
[b]Hydroponics Station
[/b]One of the new objects being added to the game is the hydroponics station. With this station, you'll be able to grow your own food right inside your spaceship or base, making food crafting much easier, especially in the early game.

[/p][previewyoutube="p1ArjG6J_u0;full"][/previewyoutube][p]

[b]All in all
[/b]Once all of these features are implemented, I’ll shift my focus to adding a main questline to the game. I’ll also be overhauling the trading system, introducing large community spaceships where players can buy and sell all kinds of items. You’ll even be able to sell your own (or stolen) spaceships there for hard cash, which you can then use to purchase new ships.[/p][p]After that, I’ll be working on bounty missions and various side quests.[/p][p]All in all, these additions will massively improve the game and make the world feel much more alive!

[/p][p]Also, if not already, please link yourself up to all social media platforms to stay up-to-date. [/p][p][url="https://discord.com/invite/NRxtpVATXa"]Discord Server[/url]

notes.title: Dev Diary 30#
notes.notes:
[b]Dear Earthlings[/b]
Just a quick update on the development of the Crew update! Things are progressing really well. The new Node AI is working like a charm, it has been thoroughly tested and debugged, and so far, it’s performing flawlessly.

[b]Recruitment[/b]
The recruitment feature has also been fully implemented. This gives the player control over a group of crew members, with two teams of up to three members each. These team members can be commanded using a new command pop-up, as seen in the video below. This system allows for more tactical gameplay, enabling players to flank enemies and execute strategic maneuvers. Just to be clear, this is separate from your crew, it's simply a group you can bring along with you.

[previewyoutube=RxzBHzcyLGg;full][/previewyoutube]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41812483/ea1456c866b872cb2b4f1371337bb69b70ff468a.png[/img]

[b]Keeping your crew members happy[/b]
Crew members now have individual needs. They require an assigned bed, enough food, and sufficient water to stay sane. If their sanity drops below a certain threshold... well, let’s just say some interesting things will happen, but I’m not going to spoil the surprise! Crew members will take care of their own needs whenever possible, ensuring they remain in good condition.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41812483/405441f5134ccdfa6ad13f56ac25eb828d503079.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41812483/fe018dea4ea2435e01e48e81eeef61f4c6f048cb.png[/img]

[b]More immersive NPC interactions[/b]
All dialogues related to crew members have also been implemented, with a total of 321 new dialogue lines added. These cover a range of interactions, including reassigning crew members to different ships, recruiting NPCs to join the crew, initiating trade, and more.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41812483/df215a64408763c3dd9693ea57f09d76f8754c1e.png[/img]

A new detainment feature has been introduced as well. Players can now detain NPCs using handcuffs, which works on all NPCs, including friendly ones and potentially unruly crew members. Exciting Update on the Game Development!

I’ve got some great news to share! I’ve fixed most of the bugs in the current version, and I’m confident that the game is now fun and fully playable until the Crew Update is released.

Speaking of the Crew Update, development officially started about a week ago. One of the biggest challenges I faced was reworking the AI and pathfinding system. Currently, AI movement is grid-based, each spaceship has its own grid, and moving an enemy from point A to B requires an enormous amount of trigonometry. However, for the Crew Update, it's essential for NPCs to move seamlessly between ships, so I needed to find a better solution.

[previewyoutube=VWGPmD4OENg;full][/previewyoutube]

After some deep problem-solving, I’ve started completely revamping the AI system, transitioning it to a node-based system. This will make the AI feel more dynamic and alive instead of being rigidly confined to a grid. It also unlocks tons of exciting possibilities for future gameplay mechanics. I’ve been experimenting with decompression and other fun features, and the early results are really promising! I’ve even put together a small test video below, it looks great, and I’m excited to see how it evolves.

notes.notes:
Hi earthlings,

As the year wraps up, it’s the perfect time to celebrate how much the game has grown and touch on a few key highlights. This year saw an incredible influx of new players, and the growth has been beyond anything I could’ve imagined!

[b]SALES[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41812483/0b436f1533c8ec73cf23dce1a6c9ab16b617c60e.png[/img]
This year, a whopping 2,838 new players joined our community, and the game raked in an incredible $30,174 in gross sales! Honestly, this completely blows my mind, I never imagined we’d achieve anything close to this!

[b]REVIEWS[/b]
I’ve received some negative reviews on the Steam store during the Winter Sale. First, I want to apologize to anyone who felt the game didn’t meet their expectations, that feedback is completely fair. I take every review to heart and always strive to improve the game.

That said, I’m just one solo developer juggling a full-time job, family life, and this passion project. I don’t have a dedicated test team. You, the players, are my amazing bug-hunters! Yes, there are bugs, some nasty ones, but with your bug reports, I’m squashing them as quickly as I can.

To make up for the rough edges, I’ve decided to reduce the game’s price by 20% after the winter sale. I think it’s only fair, and I deeply appreciate your support as I continue to make the game better for everyone.

And to everyone who left a positive review, thank you from the bottom of my heart. Your support and kind words mean the world to me and are what keep me going!

[b]CASE YELLOW LABS[/b]
Let’s end on a high note! Thanks to the game’s success, I’m taking a big step forward, I’m setting up my own business! On January 8th, I’ll officially register Case Yellow Labs at the chamber of commerce. This will be my own indie game studio! This company will be my platform for developing and publishing games, and it’s the first step toward my dream of making game development my full-time career.

Wishing everyone an amazing year ahead! I promise to keep improving the game and won’t let you down. I’m aiming for the stars, and I hope you’ll join me on this exciting journey. Here’s to a fantastic new year! 🚀

notes.title: Dev Diary 24#
notes.notes:
[b]Dear earthlings[/b],
After a very long and hard coding session which spanning across a few weeks, I am finally done with this mostly quality of life update. Although at it surface this update doesn't seem like much, there are a few new objects added, it is behind the scenes a larger one.

[b]Update[/b]
It's crucial to understand that the update released today has introduced significant changes that render all previous save files and every workshop item incompatible with the current version of the game. As a result, I had no choice but to remove them from the game. While this might seem like a drastic measure, it was a necessary step to ensure that any potential bugs or issues would not arise again. This decision wasn't taken lightly, but it was imperative for the smooth functioning of the game, especially considering the upcoming exploration update.

The new update has fundamentally altered how data is saved in the game. Previously, all game data, including save files and configurations, were stored within a single, small ini file. However, this method had its limitations, particularly as the game has grown more complex with each update. With the latest update, the game's data is now distributed across multiple files. This change may seem inconvenient, but it is a strategic move to ensure that the game can handle the addition of more content, specifically the new planets that will soon be available for exploration.

By spreading the data across multiple files, I can better manage the game's performance and stability. This approach reduces the risk of data corruption and minimizes the chances of bugs reappearing. The previous system was becoming increasingly inadequate for the game's expanding scope, and this overhaul was necessary to prepare the game for future updates. The new method of data storage not only supports the current game state but also lays the foundation for future expansions and improvements, making the game more robust and reliable.

In addition to these technical changes, I have introduced a new object called the Terminal. This addition serves multiple purposes, primarily enhancing the storytelling aspect of the game. The Terminal is designed to add a deeper narrative layer to every spaceship, providing players with more context and background as they explore the game's universe. Whether you're in the midst of a mission or tinkering in the editor mode, the Terminal offers a new way to engage with the game's story. It's a tool that can be used creatively by players to develop their own stories or to uncover hidden lore within the game.

The introduction of the Terminal is part of a broader effort to enrich the player's experience by making the game world more immersive and dynamic. As players encounter different ships, each with its own Terminal, they will uncover unique stories and secrets that add depth to the overall narrative. This feature is especially exciting for those who enjoy the storytelling aspect of games, as it opens up new possibilities for exploration and discovery.

Overall, while the latest update may have caused some disruptions with save files and workshop items, these changes were essential for the continued growth and stability of the game. The shift to a more sophisticated data storage system and the addition of the Terminal object are steps towards a more engaging and polished gaming experience. I am confident that these improvements will not only prevent future issues but also enhance the overall enjoyment of the game as it continues to evolve.

[b]Dear earthlings[/b],
It's been some time since I have done one of these, so let's do one again. I can show you some development progress!


[b]Pricing[/b]
I had a discord community member complaining about the current pricing, which I totally understand. So for the sake of clarity, openness and understanding, I will explain why the pricing is the way it is. There is actually more thought behind it than it might first appear. The main reason why the pricing is at 17,99 USD at the moment is because this is how players can support me financially. I have a wife and a little daughter to take care of. Being a full-time game developer is a long-cherished dream of mine. I am nowhere near this goal at the moment, but every sale is very much appreciated, this way I have more time to spent on actual developing the game and not on working my other full-time job to make ends meet. So from a single sale ([b]17.99 USD[/b]) I personally get around [b]6.36 EUR[/b]. The calculation is as follows. Starting at [b]17,99 USD[/b] I pay 45% V.A.T which is mandatory in the country where I am from. From the [b]9.89 USD[/b] that is left, Steam takes 30%. So I will get [b]6.92 USD[/b], with the current exchange rate will result in [b]6.36 EUR[/b].

So, do I think the game in its current state if worth [b]17,99 USD[/b]? I can simply answer that by saying no. The game is currently Early Access, meaning it is far away from being done. Some features are subject to change, will change, will be enhanced or will be deleted entirely. There are still plenty of bugs to squeeze and so forth. So for those who say, this is way too much for me, I don't want to spend this amount of money on the game, I can totally understand and I appreciate your honesty. For those people I have come up with a solution though. As some of you might already know every time when I update the game I do a week long 50% off sale, yes every major update I drop will have a 50% sale. This way, you can buy the game for what it is actually worth. In the meantime, you could wishlist the game until such a sale happens. I do hope this clear things up a bit and I hope you'll understand, if not, that is okay too. Would like to hear your take on this.

For those who did pay 17.99 USD, I want to say that I really appreciate you helping me out. I do really appreciate you believing in the game. Furthermore, I can say that I will do everything in my power to make the game be worth much more than 17,99 USD. The future ahead is very bright, the game get better and better. You need to select the hot bar slot to be able to shoot your weapon. I also added a feature where some items are or aren't stackable. Weapons, for example, are not stackable.

notes.title: Dev Diary 14#
notes.notes:
[b]MULTIPLAYER[/b]
I have reached a new point in the development of Out of Orbit. A poll on the official Discord server suggests that most of the players want Out of Orbit to have multiplayer capabilities. Well, I have some good news for those players. I am currently deep in the code to give Out of Orbit multiplayer capabilities. I am not 100% sure what I want this to look like. As usual, the community has a big say in this. I do personally believe that Out of Orbit will flourish with a multiplayer sandbox mode. Basically, it's just the same as the single-player experience, but with your friends and co-up buddies. So that is what I am currently working on. However, I have to say that things like team-deathmatch and other smaller game modes like that really intrigue me. Perhaps that will be something for the future. So, if you have any suggestions on how this new multiplayer capability is going to look, feel free to join the Discord Server and spread the news. In the meantime, I won't be updating the game until multiplayer is done. I do believe the game is pretty stable as it is. There are some bugs here and there, but nothing really serious.

As far as multiplayer development goes, I managed to create a server that other players can join. Up to four players as of now. Most games have a server-client-client-client structure, meaning that the server operates on a different application. I will implement another method. Out of Orbit will have a SERVER CLIENT - CLIENT - CLIENT structure. This means that one player will be the host of the server, and other clients can join this server. This way, you can create and join servers within the game without needing to download or install other applications.

Hi all!

I have some good news! I'm currently overhauling the Enemy AI. This way, the enemy reacts a lot more natural and individualistic.

I made a sheet that shows you how it works. The higher parts of the pyramid overrules the lower parts. Each layer in the pyramid has its own selection of states. The combination of states from the top 3 layers of the pyramid determine the lowest layer of the pyramid, which results in appropriate behavior. Basically, each enemy has its own personality.
